_comment: BERC Reconsideration Order 2026/01, dated 4 June 2026 — one day after Order 2026/22.
It amends exactly two rows. Paragraph 5.1: the increases re-fixed on 3 June for the
residential lifeline (0-50 units) and first step (0-75 units) are not made effective, and the
previous rates are restored. Paragraph 5.2: 4.63 and 5.26 remain in force from bill month
June 2026. Paragraph 5.7: all other orders and directions of Orders 2026/20 and 2026/22
remain unchanged.
This is the canonical version test. Both instruments carry the SAME billing validity — bill
month June 2026 onward — so an effective interval alone cannot order them. What separates
them is the knowledge interval: 3-4 June for the superseded rule, 4 June onward for this one.
Asking for June 2026 with no asOf returns 4.63; asking with asOf 2026-06-03 returns 5.32 and
flags it as subsequently amended.
PUBLICATION LAG, RECORDED DELIBERATELY. This order is dated 4 June 2026 on its face and was
uploaded to berc.org.bd on 24 August 2026 — eighty-one days later. Neither date alone is
usable: treating the upload as the effective date would say June and July bills ran under a
rule that did not exist, and treating it as knownFrom would ignore that BERC's notification
memo 2569 published the same decision on 4 June, which DPDC carried on its own tariff page.
knownFrom is therefore 2026-06-04 with its basis named, and publishedOn stays 2026-08-24.
Legal basis is worth noting because it shows this is a named mechanism rather than an ad hoc
reversal: BERC Act 2003 ss. 22(kha) and 34, read with regulation 13(3) of the BERC Electricity
Distribution (Retail) Tariff Regulations 2016.
